dropped.claim: enGene is an extremely high-risk pre-revenue investment facing imminent cash exhaustion: with only $50.2M in cash as of October 31, 2025, operating cash outflows of -$99.2M in FY2025, and management's explicit acknowledgment that current resources are insufficient to complete clinical development of any program, the company will require near-term dilutive financing to survive despite already burning through $122.8M of cash in a single year and diluting shareholders by 35.3% year-over-year. The company's entire commercial future depends on a single unproven clinical-stage product (detalimogene) built on novel, largely untested genetic medicine technologies in a field where only a small number of genetic medicines have ever received regulatory approval, while management candidly discloses the organization's limited experience conducting clinical trials, a material weakness in financial controls that has never been independently audited, and regulatory pathways so uncertain that positive preclinical results may not predict trial success and endpoints considered meaningful today may be rejected tomorrow.

The verified findings emphasize cash deterioration from $173.0M to $50.2M without acknowledging the company also held $152.1M in marketable securities as of October 31, 2025, representing liquid assets not captured in the cash-only analysis. The combined position of $202.3M provides substantially more runway than the $50.2M cash figure suggests, and the thesis fails to address this material omission.
